title: fii_prop_firms › Cited Findings

body: **Summary:** Alcobev companies make and brand spirits, beer and wine. Price is regulated state by state, and excise duties are often 60–80% of the consumer price. Profit comes from premiumisation (Prestige and Above spirits carry far higher margins than regular brands), gross margin over ENA/grain and glass, and A&P efficiency. Each state is effectively its own market with its own route to market (government corporations or private retail), price approvals and duty changes. Key metrics: volume by segment (P&A against regular), premium share of revenue, gross margin, EBITDA margin, A&P %, price increases secured from states, ENA/grain and glass costs, state concentration, and net debt (Radico's deleveraging). Cycle drivers: state excise policy (the Maharashtra 50–60% duty hike of June 2025 and MML policy; Karnataka; Andhra and Telangana route-to-market changes), grain and ENA prices (FCI rice for ethanol diverts supply), glass prices, consumer premiumisation, the India–UK FTA cutting Scotch duty, and weather for beer. Lead indicators: state excise revenue data, ISWAI commentary, maize/grain prices, CIABC releases, company P&A volume disclosures. Winners (Radico 2016–26 on premium mix and deleveraging; United Spirits after its Diageo clean-up, shedding popular brands) leaned into premiumisation, got state pricing approvals and avoided governance issues. Losers took state bans (Bihar 2016) or were stuck in regular-brand price wars and beer cost spikes. Valuation: P/E 50–90x for spirits leaders. Radico re-rated from ~18x to ~90x. Nov 2026: Radico Q2 FY27 P&A volume grew 36% to 5.28 mn cases (FY27 target raised to 30%) while total IMFL rose only 7%. United Spirits NSV grew only +2.8% on Maharashtra/Karnataka headwinds. Traps: a state policy shock, and paying 80x for premium growth. Sources: [1](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/radico-fy27-premium-growth-target-concall-cmw1fmdww009u31qltk2uc0ay) · [2](https://www.investywise.com/?p=124785) · [3](https://www.exchange4media.com/marketing-news/premium-pours-popular-spirits-falter-is-indias-alcobev-market-looking-at-a-divide-160107.html) · [4](https://www.zeebiz.com/india/news-maharashtra-cabinet-approves-up-to-60-liquor-duty-hike-united-spirits-radico-allied-blenders-stocks-under-pressure-368784) Links: about `case_study:radico-khaitan`

data.section: Sector playbook: Indian alcoholic beverages

title: sector_playbooks › Sector playbook: Indian alcoholic beverages

body:
**False alarm: Netflix's -$3.3 bn free cash flow** (`case_study:false-alarm-netflix-negative-fcf`, verified). FLAG: free cash flow negative for years, about -$3.0 bn (2018) and -$3.27 bn (2019, 10-K), funded by junk bonds; cash content spending ~$14.6 bn vs only ~$9.2 bn of content amortisation in 2019, so reported profit overstated cash generation. Short sellers called it a debt-funded content treadmill. CONTEXT: (1) original content is a capital asset that builds a library and global brand; the gap between cash spend and amortisation was the growth investment; (2) subscribers and engagement grew globally with low churn, and prices could be raised; (3) content spend is a fixed cost spread over a growing base, so margins would rise with scale. FCF turned positive in 2020 (COVID production pause helped) and became large later as operating margin rose toward ~30% [post-2020 FCF levels from memory, unverified]. The stock still crashed -76% in 2021-22 on the first subscriber loss. LESSON: negative FCF is benign when the spend creates a durable asset that scales over a growing, retained customer base and the cash gap shrinks as a share of revenue; it is dangerous when the spend must rise faster than revenue just to stand still.

**False alarm (on survival), real (on valuation): Tesla's losses and $12 bn of share sales** (`case_study:false-alarm-tesla-losses-dilution`, verified). FLAGS: GAAP losses every year until 2020; repeated equity raises; in 2020 alone $2 bn (Feb), $5 bn at-the-market (Sep) and $5 bn at-the-market (Dec) = $12 bn; extreme short interest; P/E >100 at the 2021 peak. CONTEXT: by mid-2019 the Model 3 ramp (~5k/week), a surprise Q3-2019 profit and the Shanghai factory built in ~10 months showed the survival risk was ending. The 2020 share sales were made after a ~650% rally at a ~$500 bn valuation, so each $5 bn was only ~1% dilution: cheap capital that fully funded new factories (Giga Texas) and removed bankruptcy risk. Dilution at a high price, for growth capex, is a gift to existing holders; dilution at a low price to survive is a transfer from them. Stock: ~$11.8 split-adjusted (Jun 2019) -> ~$414 (Nov 2021), ~35x. WHERE THE FLAG CAME TRUE: the price was mostly rerating; it fell -73% to ~$101 (Jan 2023) when auto margins fell. LESSON: measure dilution as % of shares and ask the price and purpose; separate 'will it survive?' from 'is it worth this price?'.

data.section: Method and caveats

title: literature_sweep › Method and caveats

body:
- **Three companies.** Before treating any number here as a base rate, add Transrail Lighting and Techno Electric (and perhaps Bajel / GE Vernova T&D for a product-heavy comparison).
- **Different windows.** Skipper: 10 calls (Jul-24 to Oct-26). KEC: 8 calls (Feb-25 to Nov-26). KPIL: 7 calls (Feb-25 to Aug-26), plus the Nov-26 deck. All three include the FY26 domestic tendering slowdown and the Middle East war, which helps comparability. Skipper's sample includes more FY25 promises (its easier year).
- **Different reading depth.** Skipper was read in full. KEC and KPIL were read as full opening remarks plus keyword-filtered management answers (each answer with >=3 guidance terms, and its question). Vague promises are probably under-counted for the peers, which would, if anything, raise their "vague" buckets. Numeric guidance was unlikely to be missed.
- **Company-reported actuals dominate segment checks.** Group P&L, PBT, finance cost and borrowings direction were cross-checked with screener. Segment, order-inflow and NWC figures are company figures, and some are derived (flagged in `evidence`).
- **Survivorship.** All three are large, listed and still growing. A sector base rate from survivors flatters the sector.

body:
1. **A full industry map makes S0 clean.** 0 of 809 in-band names unclassified (dd4/dd5 had 482); no hand list, no judgement. Keep the
   map refreshed with an `as_of` date.
2. **Check the bhavcopy's DATE1, not the file name.** The 24-Nov-2026 file holds 23-Nov data. Rule: the frame close is the DATE1 value.
3. **Segment margins can hide a group ROIC below the cost of equity.** India Engineering 22–24% EBITDA; group ROIC ~11.5%; ROIIC ~11%.
   When ROIIC ≈ CoE, the reverse DCF finds no growth path and the DCF-consistent exit P/E collapses to ~10x — the price is entirely a bet on
   returns on new capital. Proposed L2/L3 rule: compute group ROIC and ROIIC before reading segment margins; for any capex phase, rebuild
   payback by the utilisation route as well as management's asset-turn route (here they differ ~6x).
4. **Headline vote percentages understate minority dissent when promoters hold 75%.** 14.14% against = ~92% of non-promoter votes cast.
   Proposed L5 rule: always compute dissent as against ÷ (votes cast − promoter shares) and report it next to the headline.
5. **L40 for manufacturers: the government input is often financing.** "Debt backed by government subsidy" appears only on the call; the
   AR has no grant/subsidy note. Generalise the "external fact absent from the AR" flag to financing subsidies and policy-dated segment
   rules (solar ALMM relaxations to Dec-2026).
6. **AR disclosure quirk worth a flag:** the MD&A segment table mislabels the FY26 EBITDA column as 2024-25 (cross-foot to the KPI note).
7. **Tool notes:** `decision_card.py` takes credibility as a fraction (57 printed as "5700%" — candidate input validation); the worksheet's
   own-history temperature needs n ≥ 5 (recent IPOs get "insufficient"); the NSE pledge API returned 0 rows (SHP XBRL used); AR26 two-page
   spreads garble `pdftotext -layout` (consolidated cost lines taken from XBRL instead); no 2025–26 rating filing found on NSE/BSE.

body:
1. **Reported trailing EPS can be "cheap" because of one-off gains, not cycle position.** SHK's 18.7x reported P/E is ~36x on core
   earnings (₹63 cr of insurance realisations in TTM PBT of ₹159 cr). The v1.4 cyclicals rule (normalised 10-yr EPS) did not catch it —
   normalised 19.1x agreed with the inflated trailing number. Proposed L2 rule: before any temperature read, compute **core EPS = (EBIT ex
   other income × (1 − tax) − post-tax interest) / shares** and show trailing reported, core and normalised side by side; treat
   exceptional + other income > 25% of PBT as a "good-but-misleading" flag.
2. **When ROIIC < CoE and net debt is large, the worksheet DCF goes negative and the DCF-consistent exit P/E becomes meaningless**
   (−11.5 / −1.7 / +3.5). That is a correct reading (growth at sub-CoE returns destroys value), but the card's exit-bet table prints "n/a"
   ratios. Candidate tool change: print "DCF value below net debt → equity is an option on ROIC improving" and use the own-median column
   as the reference.
3. **L42 held a second time:** group ROIC (4.4%) first exposed what the 27% Flavours segment return hides; full-cycle ROIIC ~3% over eight
   years is the core fact. Two of two random live draws in this frame family (HARSHA, SHK) have ROIC below CoE.
4. **Category-split vote results make L42's dissent rule exact.** SHK's scrutiniser report splits promoter / institutional / non-institutional
   votes, so dissent net of promoter votes needs no assumption (~42% of non-promoter votes against a family director in 2025; headline
   5.2%). Also check whether promoters voted on their own family's re-appointment.
5. **Dates slip AND numbers miss can coexist.** Credibility 31% (−29 pts vs peers): margin guidance missed by 4–5 pts twice. L26's
   "numbers met" is a sector pattern, not a law — keep scoring numbers and dates separately.
6. **Chemicals checks (new): the China-price cycle cuts both ways inside one company** (compounder = buyer of Chinese aroma chemicals;
   ingredients arm = competitor). Pollution-board check: no structured public source; NSE/BSE keyword scans + AR found nothing, and a web
   search could not tie an MPCB "fire incident… directions" minute to the company. Candidate tool: an MPCB/GPCB/CPCB directions scraper
   keyed by unit address.
7. **S0 observation:** two consecutive draws were walk #1 with no skips. The skip rules (scheme, fraud, pledge > 50%, PEAD Q1–Q2, red
   solvency) remove a minority of names; the method is getting "typical" companies, which is the point. Keep counting.
8. **Tool notes:** `nse_fetch.py announcements` prints only 15 rows in summary mode — use `--raw`/`--out` for the full list (178 here);
   XBRL tagging moved contract-manufacturing COGS from materials (FY25) to other expenses (FY26+), which breaks a naive materials ratio;
   the AR geography table contradicts the deck; `decision_card.py` still does not validate fraction inputs (validated by hand, L42); a
   single tail-anchor weight cannot express "raise one tail, keep the other" (lesson candidate for card v1.6).
